extra_misconceptions.fact: Hands-free calls still impose heavy cognitive distraction that narrows visual scanning and slows braking reaction times.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Using a hands-free voice system eliminates the crash risk associated with cell phone conversations while driving.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Fresh air and loud music do not prevent involuntary microsleeps; pulling into a safe rest area to sleep is the only cure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rolling down the window or turning up the radio keeps a drowsy driver alert enough to finish a long highway trip safely.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Only time allows the liver to metabolize alcohol, so caffeine merely creates a wide-awake drunk driver with impaired judgment.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Drinking strong black coffee or taking a cold shower lowers a person's blood alcohol concentration before driving.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Looking straight into oncoming beams causes temporary night blindness; drivers should track the white fog line on the right.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Staring directly at oncoming headlights helps a nighttime driver track the lane edge on an unlit two-lane highway.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a driver's visual, manual, and cognitive attention during a five-second text message at 55 mph?
Why is it dangerous to drive at night when your stopping distance exceeds the illumination range of low-beam headlights?
Which physical indicator warns that a fatigued driver is entering microsleep and must pull over to rest immediately?
Under what condition does an over-the-counter allergy or cold medication impair reaction time as severely as alcohol?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Airbags are supplemental restraints designed to work with seat belts; an unbuckled occupant can strike an inflating bag at lethal speed.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Vehicle airbags provide complete collision protection on their own without needing to fasten the lap and shoulder belt.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Routing a shoulder belt under the arm drives crash forces directly into the ribs and internal organs instead of the collarbone.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tucking a shoulder belt under your arm makes a long car ride safer and more comfortable for shorter passengers.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Drivers using anti-lock brakes must press the pedal firmly and hold it down so the computer can modulate wheel slip for steering.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Anti-lock braking systems shorten stopping distance on dry pavement only when the driver pumps the brake pedal rapidly.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Crumple zones deform in a controlled way to absorb kinetic energy and lengthen impact time before forces reach the passenger cabin.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rigid steel vehicle frames that resist bending protect passengers better than modern front and rear crumple zones.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a Scout position the lap belt across the body to prevent internal organ injury during a frontal collision?
What happens to belted front-seat occupants if a single unrestrained rear passenger is thrown forward in a 40 mph crash?
What measurement confirms that a child has outgrown a belt-positioning booster seat and fits an adult vehicle seat belt?
Why is it dangerous to place a rear-facing or young child passenger in front of an active front-passenger airbag?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Drivers must inflate cold tires to the specification on the driver's door jamb placard rather than the sidewall maximum limit.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Inflating tires to the maximum pressure stamped on the tire sidewall delivers the safest grip and shortest braking distance.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Braking distance grows with the square of speed, so doubling vehicle speed quadruples the distance required to brake to a stop.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Doubling your driving speed from 30 mph to 60 mph simply doubles the distance required for the brakes to stop the vehicle.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Driving heats the air inside the tire and raises pressure, so gauges must be read when tires have cooled for at least three hours.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Checking tire pressure immediately after a highway drive gives the most accurate reading for adjusting air levels.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High beams reflect off water droplets and snow crystals directly back into the driver's eyes, whereas low beams cut under the glare.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Switching on high-beam headlights improves forward visibility when driving through dense fog or heavy falling snow.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement confirms that a tire has reached the minimum legal tread depth of 2/32 inch during a penny inspection?
Where should a Scout look on the vehicle to find the manufacturer's recommended cold inflation pressure for the tires?
What happens to the kinetic energy and braking distance of a motor vehicle when its travel speed doubles from 30 to 60 mph?
Under what condition does the standard two-second following rule fail to provide enough stopping distance behind a car?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sudden reaching motions look like a weapon threat to approaching officers; wait with hands on the wheel until asked for documents.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Unbuckling your seat belt and digging into the glove box before the officer walks up speeds up a roadside traffic stop.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bicycles are legal vehicles in every state and must ride in the same direction as motor traffic while obeying all stop signs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Bicyclists riding on public roads should travel facing oncoming cars so they can see approaching traffic more clearly.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Teen passenger restrictions reduce peer distraction and risk-taking, since each added teen passenger raises fatal crash risk.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Graduated driver licensing passenger limits exist mainly to keep teen drivers from running out of seat belts in small cars.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most state laws require moving drivable vehicles to the shoulder after a minor non-injury crash to prevent secondary collisions.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Leaving cars parked in the middle of a busy highway lane after a minor bumper tap is required until police photograph the scene.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a driver position both hands after pulling over to the right shoulder during a nighttime traffic stop?
Why is it dangerous to reach into the glove compartment for registration papers before the police officer approaches?
Which traffic regulations apply equally to a Scout riding a bicycle on a public street and a motorist driving a sedan?
Under what condition does state law allow drivers to move their vehicles out of the travel lane after a minor fender bender?

extra_misconceptions.fact: White pavement markings always separate lanes moving in the same direction, while yellow markings separate opposing traffic flows.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Broken white lane lines on a multi-lane road separate traffic moving in opposite directions on a divided highway.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Five-sided pentagon signs with fluorescent yellow-green backgrounds specifically warn drivers of school zones and school crossings.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pentagon-shaped road signs warn motorists that they are approaching an interstate highway entrance or route junction.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rumble strips create loud cabin noise and steering wheel vibration to alert distracted or drowsy drivers drifting off the roadway.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Shoulder rumble strips are milled into highway asphalt to drain rainwater away from the outer travel lane during storms.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Drivers approaching a roundabout must always yield to vehicles already circulating inside the ring and wait for a safe gap.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Entering traffic has the right-of-way over circulating vehicles when merging into a multi-lane modern roundabout.

extra_socratic_questions: Which physical indicator allows a color-blind or snow-impaired driver to identify a stop, yield, or no-passing sign instantly?
What happens to severe angle and head-on crash rates when a four-way intersection is converted into a modern roundabout?
Why is it dangerous to cross a solid yellow line on your side of a two-lane rural highway to pass a slower vehicle?
What safety role do breakaway signposts and water-filled crash attenuators play along high-speed interstate exit gores?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Retroreflective material bounces headlight beams straight back to the driver's eyes from 500 feet away, far beyond white cotton.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wearing a white T-shirt at night makes a pedestrian visible from the same distance as retroreflective tape or vests.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Heavy commercial trucks carry massive momentum and require up to 40 percent more stopping distance than a passenger automobile.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Fully loaded commercial tractor-trailers stop in a shorter distance than passenger cars because they have eighteen tires.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pedestrians without sidewalks must walk on the left shoulder facing oncoming traffic so they can see and evade approaching cars.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pedestrians walking along a country road with no sidewalks should walk with their backs to traffic on the right edge.

extra_misconceptions.fact: All traffic in both directions on an undivided road must come to a full stop until the bus retracts its stop arm and red lights.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Drivers on a two-lane road may carefully pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights if no children are visible.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement confirms the visibility gap between a pedestrian in dark clothes and one wearing retroreflective gear at night?
Where are the four major blind spots located around a commercial tractor-trailer where a passenger car disappears from view?
Under what condition may a driver travelling in the opposite direction pass a stopped school bus flashing red lights?
Why is it dangerous to squeeze a passenger car along the right curb when an eighteen-wheeler signals a right-hand turn?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Survey teams must observe from well back on a protected sidewalk or behind a barrier so they never distract drivers or risk injury.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standing directly on the street median or curb line gives Scouts the safest vantage point during a traffic volume count.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unwarranted stop signs often reduce compliance and increase rear-end collisions compared to targeted traffic-calming geometry.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Adding a four-way stop sign to any residential street automatically lowers vehicle speeds and eliminates intersections crashes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Valid traffic surveys require sampling during peak school or commuter hours with sample sizes large enough to show true patterns.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Collecting traffic observations for ten minutes on a quiet Sunday afternoon accurately represents weekday commuter hazards.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Effective community traffic safety combines the Three Es of engineering, enforcement, and education to fix root roadway hazards.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Stricter police ticketing alone solves high-crash corridors even when sightlines and crosswalk lighting remain obstructed.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a Scout position a clipboard tally team when conducting a neighborhood intersection traffic safety survey?
Which recorded metrics turn a raw thirty-minute intersection tally into an actionable traffic engineering recommendation?
What happens to the validity of a community seat belt or stop-sign survey if observers stand conspicuously in the roadway?
Which questions in an interview with a traffic officer help separate a road engineering flaw from an enforcement issue?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The field spans civil traffic engineers, crash reconstructionists, human-factors researchers, urban planners, and EMS specialists.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Traffic safety careers are limited to uniformed police officers writing speeding citations on state highways.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Reconstructionists combine skid-mark physics, crush profiles, and Event Data Recorder downloads to compute exact impact velocities.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Forensic crash reconstructionists rely primarily on eyewitness estimates to determine how fast vehicles were travelling.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Engineers must pass the Fundamentals of Engineering exam, complete four years of supervised practice, and pass the PE examination.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Graduating with a four-year civil engineering degree immediately qualifies an engineer to stamp public highway blueprints.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Signal technicians program microprocessor controllers, maintain inductive loop sensors, and synchronize corridor timing networks.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Municipal traffic signal technicians only replace burned-out light bulbs inside overhead intersection signal heads.

extra_socratic_questions: What state license must a civil engineering graduate earn before signing and sealing public roadway and signal design plans?
Which physical evidence at a collision scene allows a forensic crash reconstructionist to calculate pre-impact vehicle speed?
What specialized training separates an automated vehicle safety researcher from a municipal transportation planner?
Which daily responsibilities connect a highway patrol traffic specialist with state department of transportation engineers?
